index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure presents a hierarchical taxonomy of representative geometric methods for 3D pairwise coarse registration, structured as a tree diagram with nested branches. The global layout is a vertical tree starting from the root node at the top left, expanding downward and to the right through successive levels of categorization. The main root node is labeled 'Geometric methods (Sec. 3.1)', written in black text, with section references in red. From this root, two primary branches extend: 'Correspondence-based methods (Sec. 3.1.1)' and 'Correspondence-free methods (Sec. 3.1.2)', both also labeled with black text and red section numbers. Each branch further subdivides into subcategories connected by horizontal lines and vertical connectors, forming a clear indented hierarchy.

Under 'Correspondence-based methods', the first major subcategory is 'Keypoint detection', which splits into 'Fixed-scale keypoint detection' and 'Adaptive-scale keypoint detection'. Next is 'Descriptor', branching into 'LRF-based methods' and 'LRF-independent methods'. Following this is 'Matching technique', which leads to 'Correspondence optimization', itself divided into 'Voting-based methods' and 'Voting-free methods'. The final subcategory under correspondence-based methods is 'Transformation estimation', which includes 'RANSAC-based methods' and '4PCS-based methods'.

The second main branch, 'Correspondence-free methods', contains two subcategories: 'Hough transform methods' and 'Branch-and-bound methods'. The latter further divides into 'Decomposition-based methods' and 'Non-decomposition methods'. All nodes are represented as plain text labels without shapes or colors; connections are simple black lines—horizontal for branching and vertical for hierarchy—with no arrows, indicating a static classification rather than a process flow.

The visual style is minimalistic, using only black text on white background, with section references highlighted in red for emphasis. There are no icons, symbols, or mathematical equations within the diagram. The caption at the bottom reads: 'Fig 1. Taxonomy of representative geometric methods', providing context that this is a classification scheme for methods used in 3D pairwise coarse registration. The structure reflects a logical progression from general to specific, grouping methods based on whether they rely on point correspondences and then further refining each group by technical approach.
